paragraphs.text: Be ye imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
paragraphs.original: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mimētai mou ginesthe, kathōs kagō Christou.

paragraphs.text: Now I praise you that ye remember me in all things, and hold fast the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.
paragraphs.original: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε.
paragraphs.translit: Epainō de hymas hoti panta mou memnēsthe kai kathōs paredōka hymin tas paradoseis katechete.

paragraphs.text: But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.
paragraphs.original: θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: thelō de hymas eidenai hoti pantos andros hē kephalē ho Christos estin, kephalē de gynaikos ho anēr, kephalē de tou Christou ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoreth his head.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: pas anēr proseuchomenos ē prophēteuōn kata kephalēs echōn kataischynei tēn kephalēn autou·

paragraphs.text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head unveiled dishonoreth her head; for it is one and the same thing as if she were shaven.
paragraphs.original: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτῆς, ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ.
paragraphs.translit: pasa de gynē proseuchomenē ē prophēteuousa akatakalyptō tē kephalē kataischynei tēn kephalēn autēs, hen gar estin kai to auto tē exyrēmenē.

paragraphs.text: For if a woman is not veiled, let her also be shorn: but if it is a shame to a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be veiled.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή, καὶ κειράσθω· εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι, κατακαλυπτέσθω.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar ou katakalyptetai gynē, kai keirasthō· ei de aischron gynaiki to keirasthai ē xyrasthai, katakalyptesthō.

paragraphs.text: For a man indeed ought not to have his head veiled, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.
paragraphs.original: ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν, εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα θεοῦ ὑπάρχων· ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: anēr men gar ouk opheilei katakalyptesthai tēn kephalēn, eikōn kai doxa theou hyparchōn· hē gynē de doxa andros estin.

paragraphs.text: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man:
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός·
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin anēr ek gynaikos, alla gynē ex andros·

paragraphs.text: for neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man:
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar ouk ektisthē anēr dia tēn gynaika, alla gynē dia ton andra.

paragraphs.text: for this cause ought the woman to have [a sign of] authority on her head, because of the angels.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto opheilei hē gynē exousian echein epi tēs kephalēs dia tous angelous.

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless, neither is the woman without the man, nor the man without the woman, in the Lord.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν οὔτε γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς ἐν κυρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: plēn oute gynē chōris andros oute anēr chōris gynaikos en kyriō·

paragraphs.text: For as the woman is of the man, so is the man also by the woman; but all things are of God.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός, οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός· τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar hē gynē ek tou andros, houtōs kai ho anēr dia tēs gynaikos· ta de panta ek tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Judge ye in yourselves: is it seemly that a woman pray unto God unveiled?
paragraphs.original: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε· πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: en hymin autois krinate· prepon estin gynaika akatakalypton tō theō proseuchesthai;

paragraphs.text: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ, ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: oude hē physis autē didaskei hymas hoti anēr men ean koma, atimia autō estin,

paragraphs.text: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.
paragraphs.original: γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ, δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν; ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου δέδοται.
paragraphs.translit: gynē de ean koma, doxa autē estin; hoti hē komē anti peribolaiou dedotai.

paragraphs.text: But if any man seemeth to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι, ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de tis dokei philoneikos einai, hēmeis toiautēn synētheian ouk echomen, oude hai ekklēsiai tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But in giving you this charge, I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better but for the worse.
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτο δὲ παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: Touto de parangellōn ouk epainō hoti ouk eis to kreisson alla eis to hēsson synerchesthe.

paragraphs.text: For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that divisions exist among you; and I partly believe it.
paragraphs.original: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.
paragraphs.translit: prōton men gar synerchomenōn hymōn en ekklēsia akouō schismata en hymin hyparchein, kai meros ti pisteuō.

paragraphs.text: For there must be also factions among you, that they that are approved may be made manifest among you.
paragraphs.original: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: dei gar kai haireseis en hymin einai, hina kai hoi dokimoi phaneroi genōntai en hymin.

paragraphs.text: When therefore ye assemble yourselves together, it is not possible to eat the Lord`s supper:
paragraphs.original: συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: synerchomenōn oun hymōn epi to auto ouk estin kyriakon deipnon phagein,

paragraphs.text: for in your eating each one taketh before [other] his own supper; and one is hungry, and another is drunken.
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.
paragraphs.translit: hekastos gar to idion deipnon prolambanei en tō phagein, kai hos men peina, hos de methyei.

paragraphs.text: What, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and put them to shame that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you? In this I praise you not.
paragraphs.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν; ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε, καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας; τί εἴπω ὑμῖν; ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς; ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ.
paragraphs.translit: mē gar oikias ouk echete eis to esthiein kai pinein; ē tēs ekklēsias tou theou kataphroneite, kai kataischynete tous mē echontas; ti eipō hymin; epainesō hymas; en toutō ouk epainō.

paragraphs.text: For I received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus in the night in which he was betrayed took bread;
paragraphs.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον
paragraphs.translit: Egō gar parelabon apo tou kyriou, ho kai paredōka hymin, hoti ho kyrios Iēsous en tē nykti hē paredideto elaben arton

paragraphs.text: and when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, This is my body, which is for you: this do in remembrance of me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eucharistēsas eklasen kai eipen· Touto mou estin to sōma to hyper hymōn· touto poieite eis tēn emēn anamnēsin.

paragraphs.text: In like manner also the cup, after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood: this do, as often as ye drink [it], in remembrance of me.
paragraphs.original: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
paragraphs.translit: hōsautōs kai to potērion meta to deipnēsai, legōn· Touto to potērion hē kainē diathēkē estin en tō emō haimati· touto poieite, hosakis ean pinēte, eis tēn emēn anamnēsin.

paragraphs.text: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink the cup, ye proclaim the Lord`s death till he come.
paragraphs.original: ὁσάκις γὰρ ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ.
paragraphs.translit: hosakis gar ean esthiēte ton arton touton kai to potērion pinēte, ton thanaton tou kyriou katangellete, achri hou elthē.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore whosoever shall eat the bread or drink the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner, shall be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ κυρίου ἀναξίως, ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: Hōste hos an esthiē ton arton ē pinē to potērion tou kyriou anaxiōs, enochos estai tou sōmatos kai tou haimatos tou kyriou.

paragraphs.text: But let a man prove himself, and so let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.
paragraphs.original: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν, καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω·
paragraphs.translit: dokimazetō de anthrōpos heauton, kai houtōs ek tou artou esthietō kai ek tou potēriou pinetō·

paragraphs.text: For he that eateth and drinketh, eateth and drinketh judgment unto himself, if he discern not the body.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ σῶμα.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar esthiōn kai pinōn krima heautō esthiei kai pinei mē diakrinōn to sōma.

paragraphs.text: For this cause many among you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄρρωστοι καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto en hymin polloi astheneis kai arrōstoi kai koimōntai hikanoi.

paragraphs.text: But if we discerned ourselves, we should not be judged.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἑαυτοὺς διεκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα·
paragraphs.translit: ei de heautous diekrinomen, ouk an ekrinometha·

paragraphs.text: But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
paragraphs.original: κρινόμενοι δὲ ὑπὸ κυρίου παιδευόμεθα, ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν.
paragraphs.translit: krinomenoi de hypo kyriou paideuometha, hina mē syn tō kosmō katakrithōmen.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, wait one for another.
paragraphs.original: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, συνερχόμενοι εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν ἀλλήλους ἐκδέχεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: Hōste, adelphoi mou, synerchomenoi eis to phagein allēlous ekdechesthe.

paragraphs.text: If any man is hungry, let him eat at home; that your coming together be not unto judgment. And the rest will I set in order whensoever I come.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις πεινᾷ, ἐν οἴκῳ ἐσθιέτω, ἵνα μὴ εἰς κρίμα συνέρχησθε. Τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ὡς ἂν ἔλθω διατάξομαι.
paragraphs.translit: ei tis peina, en oikō esthietō, hina mē eis krima synerchēsthe. Ta de loipa hōs an elthō diataxomai.
